page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture utilizing a dedicated AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core metrics placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is mixed; while large-block write bandwidth and PassMark memory scores are average, read-only small-block cached memory bandwidth is poor, landing in the bottom 10%. Cryptographic and vector instruction capabilities are supported via hardware flags like AVX-512 and AES, though PassMark CPU encryption and extended instruction tests register in the lower 25%.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.g8a.large offers a stable entry-level resource profile for general-purpose workloads. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for applications requiring consistent single-threaded execution rather than highly parallelized compute or intensive database operations, where PassMark database benchmarks and Redis SET operations show lower performance. Suitable workloads include lightweight web serving, text processing, single-threaded utility scripts, and basic development environments.
